name: Schedule upload and import
summary: Uploading a construction schedule file, tracking its processing, keeping a history of uploads, and telling people when processing finishes.

roles.note: The seed catalog has no schedule-specific permission strings. Who may upload or edit schedules is unknown (DEC-010 covers related edit rights).

nfr.statement: Time from finishing a schedule upload to its planned dates showing in the timeline.
nfr.open_question: How long may processing take for a large schedule, for example several thousand tasks?

requirements.title: Upload a project schedule
requirements.statement: Users with the right permissions can upload a project schedule from a dedicated Schedule section, to get better insight into progress. Schedules can be uploaded and downloaded in several formats, up to 750 MB. A schedule is optional.

sources.title: Product walkthrough and clarifications recorded in the 2026-10-28 ledger

acceptance_criteria.given: A project user with schedule permission
acceptance_criteria.when: They upload a supported schedule file
acceptance_criteria.then: The upload is accepted for processing

acceptance_criteria.given: A user opens Schedule in a project's side panel
acceptance_criteria.then: They can upload a new schedule file and see a log of earlier uploads
The schedule is reflected in the project accurately

requirements.title: Uploading a schedule file is not the same as importing its tasks
requirements.statement: When a schedule file finishes uploading, it is marked as processing and people are notified. Whether processing later succeeds or fails is recorded separately. A finished upload doesn't mean any tasks became planned dates.
open_checks: The parser and task-mapping code is still not located (2026-10-29: not in api-2d-progress; p6-reader is only a local experiment)

acceptance_criteria.given: A schedule file whose upload has finished
acceptance_criteria.then: Its status becomes processing and the uploader is notified

requirements.title: Schedule version history
requirements.statement: Every schedule update is kept as a version, and users can view earlier versions and compare them with the latest.

acceptance_criteria.given: A schedule has been updated twice
acceptance_criteria.then: They see all three versions and can compare any with the latest

requirements.title: Upload details, and email when processing finishes
requirements.statement: Each uploaded schedule shows who uploaded it, when, and its status. When its status changes to success or failed, the uploader and the project admins are emailed.

acceptance_criteria.given: A user on a project's Schedule page
acceptance_criteria.then: They see the uploader's name, the upload date and the status, and optionally the changes from the previous schedule

acceptance_criteria.given: A schedule's status changes to Success or Failed
acceptance_criteria.then: The uploader and the project admins are emailed

requirements.title: Abandoned schedule uploads are cancelled when the list is read
requirements.statement: When the upload list is read (newest first), any upload still "created" after 15 minutes is shown as cancelled, and the database is updated in the background.

acceptance_criteria.given: A schedule upload created 20 minutes ago that never uploaded
acceptance_criteria.then: It is shown as cancelled, and its stored status becomes cancelled
